title: Fresh fish and Reptimers: prison terms for new and old inmates
summary: Maxey explains that a fresh fish is a newcomer and old hands are called Reptimers, Lifetimers or old Ace; Allen checks the pronunciation.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Well, fresh fish is always called a man that's first coming in the penitentiary. Probably it's his second time here. But what makes them call him a fresh fish because it's been quite a while since he was here. He's not used to the place like them that's already here. That's why they call him a fresh fish. Well, what's the opposite of fresh fish? Well, I mean, what you mean by what is obvious because of fresh fish?
Well, I mean, somebody who's been here a long time.

What do you call him? Well, a fella's been here for a long time. Some of them call him old Reptimers. Some of them call him Lifetimers. Some of them call him old Ace. Well, you know that he's not a fresh fish.
Reptimers? Say that again for a minute. I want to get the pronunciation.
Well, lots of times they call a man who's been here a long time, they call him a Reptimer.
Is that like R-A-P, like you rap on a guitar?
Well, not exact. It's not Reptimers. It's not Reptimers.
Rep, like a Reptile. It's a Rep. It's a Rep, Rep, Reptimers.
